newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials firmer in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials firmer in active trade.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index added 157.3 to a new all-time high of 11,698.83 in active trade on Tuesday, brokers said.

But they added that they expected the current bull run on the bourse to taper off after Thursday's announcement of a national annual budget, whose contents they said might have a dampening effect on investors.
"I don't think it (the bull run) is sustainable. We don't expect anything much from the budget and the market will probably only remain strong until Friday," one broker said.
However, on Monday some market analysts had said they expected the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange to defy traditional trends and keep on a firm path ahead of the budget which they expected to be positive.

Counters to trade firmer on Tuesday included blue-chip conglomerate Delta which lept 100 cents to 2,200 while retail and hotel giant Meikles added 40 cents to 3,150 and bank NMB was up 25 cents to 3,550.
Food processor Natfood and sugar growers Hippo both put on 20 cents to 340 and 1,800 respectively.

Mining firms continued to be lifeless with most counters trading at previous levels, though gold producer Rio Tinto lost 100 cents to 1,900. The seven share mining index slipped 7.95 points to close at 825.29.
